explain.say: Have you ever voted for a class monitor or a team captain? A country's election works the same way, just much bigger. An election is when people choose leaders by voting. Look at the checklist: six steps, from signing up to the winners starting work.

explain.say: See the first step ticked: register to vote. That means putting your name on the official list of voters. In most countries you can vote from 18; in Brazil, Austria and Argentina you can start at 16. How old will you be when you can vote?

explain.say: Next, candidates campaign. A candidate is a person who wants to be chosen. They give speeches, knock on doors and explain their promises. Smart voters compare those ideas carefully. What promise would you want to hear?

explain.say: Now the key step: vote in secret. Alone in a booth, you mark a paper or press a button on a machine, like India's electronic voting machines. Secret means nobody can pressure you or see your choice. Why do you think that matters?

faq.a: Usually adult citizens, most often from age 18. A few countries, such as Brazil, Austria and Argentina, allow voting from 16. You normally need to be on the voters list.
A secret ballot means nobody can see how you voted, so nobody can bully, bribe or punish you for your choice. It helps everyone vote freely.
Officials from an independent election body count the votes, like the Election Commission of India. Watchers from each party, and sometimes international observers, check it is fair.
A candidate is a person who stands in an election hoping to be chosen. Many belong to a political party, a group with shared ideas, but some stand alone as independents.
In most countries voting is your free choice. In some, like Australia, Belgium and Brazil, adults must vote or may pay a small fine.

facts: Voting is compulsory for adults in Australia, Belgium and Brazil.
India has used electronic voting machines in every national election since 2004.
